name: Wetting brush

guide.summary: Wet the gel and sediment under the brush.
guide.biology: Misting a drying culture plate brings back its moisture without washing anything away.
guide.rules: Each covered gel or sediment cell has its moisture set to 0.9; water cells always have moisture 1 and are left alone. It adds no water and dilutes nothing: every amount in the cell stays the same. Drying never concentrates chemicals: amounts are kept per cell, so a drying cell holds exactly what it held.
guide.example: Wet a strip of drying gel and compare the organisms on it with those beside it.

where: Gel and sediment cells (water cells are always fully wet and are left alone).
changes: Only the moisture of each covered gel and sediment cell.
doesNotChange: Adds no water and dilutes nothing: every amount in the cell stays the same. Drying never concentrates chemicals: amounts are kept per cell, so a drying cell holds exactly what it held.
watchFor: Whether organisms that were slowing down on drying gel or sediment pick up again.
